pr_title: roachtest: ensure workload node has same zone as cluster if unspecified
pr_body:
Previously we randomized the default zones for gce when unspecified to avoid zone exhaustion errors. However, this ran into an issue with workload nodes which are created seperately from the main cluster, as a different default zone would return for each.

This change exposes the zone randomization logic up to roachtest so it can assign the same default zone for both CRDB cluster and workload node

Fixes: cockroachdb#129997
Release note: none
Epic: none
pr_comments: This change is [](https://reviewable.io/reviews/cockroachdb/cockroach/130083)
Didn't end up moving the zone randomization up to roachtest, since we still want roachprod clusters created via CLI to have randomized zones. Let me know if I'm missing something though.

issue_context.title: roachtest: increase in network cost due to the change "support custom workload node CPU sizes" #125648
issue_context.body:
The recent changes to [support custom workload node CPU sizes](https://github.com/cockroachdb/cockroach/pull/125648) seems to have caused an increase in the cost in "Network Inter Zone Data Transfer Out".

As per the analysis, the reason is that the cluster and the workload cluster can get created in different zones which is adding up to the data transfer cost.



Jira issue: CRDB-41829

review_comments: Maybe we should do the same thing for the cases of `len(zones) == 0 && (cloud == AWS || cloud == Azure)`? Otherwise, the default zone assignment logic is deferred to the corresponding `Create`, but only in those cases.

Done.

Did find one small but annoying thing about azure is they split up regions (i.e. us-east) and availability zones (i.e. 1), but we assume that zone = combination of both. Azure already doesn't work for multi-region ([issue here](https://github.com/cockroachdb/cockroach/issues/124612)) so i left it as is but something to keep in mind.
Let's add a comment to make it clear that it's a regression test, along with the GH issue reference.
